title: Fix NAT gateway availability zone assumptions (route table -> NAT mapping)
author: Victor Alvarez
body:
Context: During dogfood of the alpha VPC module in the Redwood sandbox account (ENG-4895), we hit a failure where private subnet route tables were pointing at a NAT gateway that either did not exist or lived in a different AZ. The root cause was an implicit assumption in the VPC module that the number/order of public subnets == number/order of private subnets and that NAT gateways can be indexed by position (count/index) rather than by AZ identity.

Problem: When customers (or our own example env) use a non-symmetric subnet layout (e.g., 3 private subnets across 3 AZs but only 2 public subnets, or `single_nat_gateway = true`), the existing logic would still attempt to attach each private route table to `aws_nat_gateway.nat[index]`. In the single NAT case, `index > 0` would reference a NAT that was never created; in the uneven-AZ case the mapping could silently route a private subnet to a NAT in another AZ.

What changed: This PR switches NAT GW + route mapping from positional indexing to an AZ-keyed mapping derived from the actual `public_subnets_by_az` map. For `single_nat_gateway = true`, we deterministically select the first public subnet AZ (sorted) and route all private route tables to that NAT. For multi-NAT, we create one NAT per AZ that has a public subnet and only create private routes for private subnets in AZs that have a NAT; we also surface a clearer validation error when a private subnet is declared in an AZ without a corresponding public subnet (unless single NAT is enabled).

Why this is safe: It preserves the default (symmetric, one NAT per AZ) behavior, but stops producing invalid references and makes unsupported layouts fail fast with an actionable error message.

Notes: Linked discussion and repro screenshots are in the eng-infra Slack thread (see link above). This also updates the integration test harness to cover (1) 2-AZ layout with 3 private subnets and (2) single NAT layout.

Checklist: - [x] Reproduced in dogfood env before fix - [x] Added/updated tests in `tests/` harness - [x] `terraform fmt` / `validate` - [x] Updated module README caveats on supported subnet topologies - [x] Confirmed no output name changes (outputs are stable; values may change in edge cases where previous mapping was incorrect)

Follow-ups (post-merge): 1) Add a docs snippet in the deployment guide clarifying supported subnet/AZ layouts and when to use `single_nat_gateway` (owner: DevEx) 2) Consider a dedicated variable to explicitly choose "central NAT AZ" for single-NAT mode instead of relying on sorted AZ selection (owner: Infra) 3) Add a Checkov suppression note for the new validation resources if needed (owner: CI) 4) Ensure example tfvars for design partners do not specify mismatched public/private AZ lists (owner: SE/PS).
commits: vpc: key NAT gateway resources by AZ instead of index
vpc: route table association uses az->nat map (single and multi NAT modes)
vpc: add validation for private subnet AZs without public NAT (unless single_nat_gateway)
tests: add uneven subnet count scenario + single NAT scenario
docs: clarify NAT/AZ behavior and supported layouts
changed_areas: modules/vpc/main.tf (NAT gateway creation + private route mapping)
.github/workflows/ci.yml (timeout bump for integration job due to added scenario)
review_conversation: Irene Choi: Can we avoid relying on list ordering for picking the AZ in single NAT mode? Sorted AZ keys seems okay but I'd like it called out explicitly.

Victor Alvarez (author): Yep — added a note in README under `single_nat_gateway` describing how the "central" AZ is selected and why. Also added a follow-up task to consider an explicit input for this.
Nina Petrova: For EKS private control plane, are we okay routing all private subnets to a single NAT from any AZ? Some customers care about cross-AZ charges but functionally this should work.

Victor Alvarez (author): Correct — functionally okay, cross-AZ data charges are a trade-off in single NAT mode. The default remains one NAT per AZ. I added wording that single NAT is cost-optimized but not AZ-optimized.
Sahana Iyer: The integration test job is now ~23 minutes. OK for main branch, but do we still plan to keep this per-PR?
Victor Alvarez (author): For now yes; this is still within our budgeted CI runtime. If it creeps up, we can split "full" integration tests to nightly per ADR-028; not changing that policy in this PR.
Irene Choi: Approved once validation errors include the AZ name(s) to make it debuggable.
Victor Alvarez (author): Added AZ list to the error message and included the configured public/private AZ sets in the output.
release_notes: Bugfix: NAT gateway / private route mapping no longer relies on positional subnet indexing; mapping is AZ-aware.
Single NAT mode now routes all private subnets to a deterministic "central" NAT (based on sorted public subnet AZs) and documents the cross-AZ trade-off.
Improved validation and error messages for mismatched public/private subnet AZ configurations.
Integration tests expanded to cover uneven subnet counts and single NAT scenarios.
